source.title: De-attribute to Forget for LLM Unlearning
source.authors: Xin-Yang Lu; Jiabao Pan; Rachael Hwee Ling Sim; See-Kiong Ng; A. K. H. Tung; K. Low

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether paraphrased prompts and subsequent fine-tuning recover forgotten material. Its results and discussion argue that recovery depends on the unlearning method: DareU resists these tests better than several baselines, while some baselines recover rapidly during relearning.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for paraphrased-query probing and fine-tuning on the forget set after unlearning. It does not test activation-direction ablation, quantization, unrelated or small relearning sets, or prompting by jailbreak, language change, or in-context information. Values in Figure 7 are not stated numerically; the text's qualitative descriptions are recorded separately.
record.test_reason: DareU is a new unlearning method. In appendix F.5.3 and F.5.4 it is attacked with paraphrased forget queries and with relearning on DF, following the WMDP relearning setup. The study reports these results for DareU and seven baselines on Llama2-7B × TOFU. The results bear on A, B, E and F (a new method claiming to resist attacks), and the authors argue that recovery depends on the method.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct, but the paper's main conclusion is that DareU best balances forget quality and utility (highest ToW). The robustness claims are an appendix result limited to Llama2 × TOFU. In them, DareU resists paraphrase probing and resists relearning more than GA, NPO and IDK, while falling short of Retraining.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes attribution-reward PPO unlearning (DareU), rather than testing the claim's named methods as its central intervention. It tests paraphrased-query probing and fine-tuning on the forget set after unlearning.
record.method_sensitivity: Relearning outcome varies by unlearning method: the text reports rapid recovery for GA, NPO, and IDK, while DareU shows stronger resistance.
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The relearning curves are figure-only and are not accompanied by numerical values in the text. The relearning experiment fine-tunes on DF, so it does not establish whether a small or unrelated set suffices. The paraphrased-query test covers only that prompt variation.

untested.parts: No near-chance multiple-choice accuracy on hazardous knowledge (TOFU ROUGE is used instead). Attacks were run only on Llama2 × TOFU, not on Qwen3 or ArXiv.
No small, unrelated, loosely related or subset relearning sets: relearning uses the full forget set DF.
Entirely untested: no direction ablation and no access-versus-deletion analysis.
Only paraphrased queries were tested; no jailbreaks, other languages or in-context information.
DareU was not tested against quantization, activation ablation, jailbreaks or small or unrelated relearning sets.

missing.what: Utility (DR and Dtest ROUGE) for the attacked methods, needed to judge A's 'keeping general ability'. Examples: GA DR 0.001, SCRUB 0.302, NPO 0.318, DareU 0.797.
Gibberish rates showing GA's low forget ROUGE reflects collapse (GA 100%, SCRUB 45%, NPO 24%, DareU 4%).

record.verdict_notes: The reader's version ids V1, V2 and V5 were invalid and have been remapped. F is tested, because DareU is a new method claiming robustness to paraphrase and relearning; the reader marked it not_tested. The relearning results are figure-only and qualitative. Relearning on the full forget set is a stronger attack than B's small-set framing. The paraphrase test uses ROUGE, where even the Original model scores only 0.522 on paraphrases, which limits its sensitivity.

versions.untested_parts: The study evaluates recovery after paraphrased queries and relearning, but does not establish near-chance targeted-knowledge accuracy or test every attack named in the version.
Relearning uses the forget set DF, not a small, unrelated, loosely related, or explicitly limited subset of forgotten facts.
No activation-direction ablation or internal access-versus-deletion test is reported.
No low-bit quantization attack is reported.
The study tests paraphrased queries only; it does not test jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
The paper does not claim or test a counter-method against the full set of attacks in the claim.

tranche.reason: T5 accepts results as well as arguments. Table 19 shows paraphrasing restores nothing for any unlearner (E absent), and Fig 7/F.5.4 show DareU only partly resists relearning (F partial). T2 is also defensible, but the given call fits the rule.

source_check.notes: Table 19/20 values verified. Relearning (R13, R16, R17, R19) is figure-only: full DF (400 TOFU forget10 samples), 0-50 steps, Retraining curve in Fig 7. Low paraphrase ROUGE partly reflects collapse for GA (100% gibberish), SCRUB (45%) and NPO (24%). Several statements cite this study's rows without naming it.

statements.problem: Nothing wrong. The study is not named and is cited only through R13 (GA rapidly recovers after relearning on the full DF, figure-only), and that matches F.5.4.

Nothing wrong. The study is not named and is cited only through R19. 'Cuts recovery without removing it' matches the text: stronger resistance than GA/NPO/IDK, short of Retraining. DareU is a standalone objective, not an add-on.
Correct per Table 19: GA 0.000, IDK 0.033, SCRUB 0.209, NPO 0.230, SCRN 0.277, DareU 0.321, GDiff 0.334 vs Retraining 0.348. GA's 0.000 reflects collapse (100% gibberish).
Nothing wrong. The study is not named and is cited only through R4. GA's zero paraphrase ROUGE does come with collapse: DR ROUGE 0.001, Dtest 0.000, 100% gibberish (Tables 19-20).
Correct: NPO paraphrased ROUGE 0.230 vs Retraining 0.348 (Table 19). Caveat not stated: NPO here also has DR ROUGE 0.318 and 23.58% gibberish (Table 20).
Nothing wrong. The study is not named and is cited only through R10 (DareU 0.321 vs Retraining 0.348). Every baseline here also shows no paraphrase recovery, and this study is ICML, not a preprint.

statements.problem: The text does not support 'recovers a large share' for DareU. It stresses stronger resistance than GA/NPO/IDK, short of Retraining, gives no magnitude, and relearning used the full DF.
